summary: Content search feature filter never matches most product feature ids
description:
ContentDocument indexes the product features of a content as a single tokenized "feature" field, so the StandardAnalyzer lowercases the ids and splits them on hyphens, while the ecommerce and lucene content searches look each selected feature id up with a TermQuery on the raw id. A feature filter therefore only matches all-digit ids; ids like {{STANDARD}} or {{Y1990}} never match. In the lucene admin search the typed feature fields (SEARCH_FEAT, SEARCH_FEAT2, SEARCH_FEAT3) are also ignored unless a feature is selected in a dropdown as well, because their query is only added inside the {{featureIdByType}} block, and AdminSearch.ftl redisplays SEARCH_FEAT in all three fields.

Index one untokenized field per feature id, always add the feature query when a feature is given, and redisplay each field's own value.

summary: ListProductTag updates every row regardless of the select checkbox
description:
The {{ListProductTag}} multi form in {{ProductForms.xml}} shows a select checkbox on each row but does not set {{use-row-submit="true"}}, so {{ServiceMultiEventHandler}} calls {{updateProductKeyword}} for every row whether it is ticked or not. A status changed on an unticked row is still applied, and ticking a row has no effect.

h3. Proposed change

Add {{use-row-submit="true"}} to the form so only the ticked rows are submitted, as other multi forms in the same file already do.

summary: Remove the unused shutdown trap and stop-signal script from the Docker image
description:
The Docker entrypoint registers {{trap shutdown_ofbiz SIGTERM SIGINT}}, which runs {{send_ofbiz_stop_signal.sh}} to send SHUTDOWN to the admin port, but the script ends with {{exec "$@"}}, so the OFBiz JVM replaces the shell and receives the stop signal directly; {{docker stop}} already shuts OFBiz down gracefully through its shutdown hook. The trap therefore never runs, and {{send_ofbiz_stop_signal.sh}} is the only reason {{curl}} is installed in the image.

Remove the trap, the shutdown_ofbiz function, the send_ofbiz_stop_signal.sh script and the curl package.

summary: One JobSandbox row with sub-millisecond runTime stalls the whole job poller
description:
The {{PersistedServiceJob}} constructor always parses {{JobSandbox.runTime}} as a string with a formatter that accepts at most 3 fractional digits, even when {{runTimeEpoch}} is set and the parsed value is not used. A {{runTime}} with microsecond or nanosecond precision, for example written by SQL on PostgreSQL where {{now()}} has microseconds, throws a {{DateTimeParseException}} ("unparsed text found at index 23").

The exception is thrown from {{JobManager.poll()}}, which rolls back the whole poll and returns no jobs. The row is polled again on the next cycle, so a single such row stops every scheduled job indefinitely, with only a warning in the log.

The same formatter also reads the fraction as microseconds instead of milliseconds, so a normal {{.123}} value loses its 123 ms.

h3. Proposed change

Use {{runTimeEpoch}} when it is set, and otherwise take the epoch directly from the {{runTime}} timestamp ({{getTimestamp("runTime").getTime()}}) instead of formatting it to a string and parsing it back. This handles any precision, keeps the milliseconds and avoids the daylight saving ambiguity of a wall-clock string. The formatter is then unused and is removed.

h3. Release branch

release24.09 has the same code (introduced by OFBIZ-12864), so the fix should be backported.

summary: Disable Groovy @Grab in the ProgramExport and GroovyUtil script sandboxes
description:
ProgramExport tries to disable Groovy's @Grab support by loading {{org.codehaus.groovy.transform.GrabAnnotationTransformation}}, but that class is actually {{groovy.grape.GrabAnnotationTransformation}} (in Groovy 3, 5 and 6). The resulting {{ClassNotFoundException}} is silently ignored, so @Grab and @GrabResolver annotations in a submitted script are still processed at compile time, before the SecureASTCustomizer checks run.

The sandboxed compiler configurations in {{GroovyUtil}} do not disable @Grab either.

On trunk, Groovy 6 brings Apache Ivy onto the runtime classpath through {{groovy-grape-ivy}}, so a script can resolve and load artifacts from an arbitrary repository. OFBiz does not use @Grab anywhere.

h3. Proposed changes

* ProgramExport: reference {{groovy.grape.GrabAnnotationTransformation}} directly, so the transform is always disabled and a future rename breaks the build instead of silently doing nothing.
* GroovyUtil: disable the same transform in both sandboxed compiler configurations.
* dependencies.gradle: exclude {{groovy-grape-ivy}} from {{groovy-all}}, as is already done for {{groovy-grape-maven}}, so no Grape engine is on the runtime classpath.

h3. Release branch

release24.09 has the same wrong class name, but Groovy 3.0.25 declares Ivy as an optional dependency, so it is not on the runtime classpath and @Grab cannot resolve anything there. Trunk only.

summary: Ecommerce pages fail to render links when OFBiz runs with a port offset
Ecommerce content search never finds anything because the Lucene content index has wrong site terms
description:
The ecommerce content search requires the term site:WebStoreCONTENT, but ContentDocument fills the site field from the WEB_SITE_PUB_PT contents it finds by following ContentAssoc from contentId to contentIdTo, i.e. the descendants of the indexed content, not its ancestors. It also joins them into a single non-tokenized StringField, so even a correct list of more than one ancestor never matches a term query. As a result the storefront content search returns nothing on demo data.

The fix walks the content associations upwards and adds one site field per ancestor publish point.

2) Now approve the order and depress on " Pack Shipment for shipgroup"

4) Now go on Order detail page

summary: Order Item "Remaining" duplicates "Outstanding"
description:
In the quantities relating to order items, there are two numbers presented: "remaining" and "outstanding". The calculations for these two numbers are identical.

Compare

[https://github.com/apache/ofbiz-framework/blame/trunk/applications/order/template/order/OrderItems.ftl#L252]
for a purchase order item (and two lines below for a sales order item)

with

[https://github.com/apache/ofbiz-framework/blame/trunk/applications/order/template/order/OrderItems.ftl#L303] for a purchases order item (and two lines below for a sales order item)

The only difference I can see between the Remaining and Outstanding numbers is the extra test the second time to force the outstanding number to zero for a status of ITEM_COMPLETED.

There are two different numbers because the original intent was that Remaining is the quantity after any cancellations, so in the common situation where there have been no cancellations, Remaining should be the same as the original quantity ordered.

A bug was introduced in a commit a long time ago, where "Remaining" was changed so it replicates "Outstanding".

summary: Docker images keep a stale JDK because Dependabot never refreshes the eclipse-temurin digest
description:
The Dockerfile pins the base image as eclipse-temurin:<major>@sha256:<digest>. Because a newer Temurin major is always available, Dependabot only opens major tag bumps (17 to 18, 19, ... 25), which we close, and never opens a digest refresh within the pinned major. As a result the release24.09 images still build on JDK 17.0.10 from January 2024, and trunk's Java 25 pin will go stale the same way.

The fix adds a semver-major ignore for eclipse-temurin to both docker entries in .github/dependabot.yml, so Dependabot keeps the digest current within the pinned major, and refreshes the release24.09 Dockerfile digest once.

summary: createDataResource will sometimes fail when uploading Excel documents due to missing libraries
description:
createDataResource calls org.ofbiz.content.data.DataResourceWorker.getMimeTypeWithByteBuffer().  getMimeTypeWithByteBuffer calls into the Tika library to detect the mime type of the file.  Tika will try to detect the file format, leveraging a number of detectors, one of which is Apache POI.  Apache POI's detector will try to call routines in jar files that are not included in with the content application, leading to the following exception:

java.lang.IllegalAccessError: tried to access method org.apache.poi.util.POILogger.log(ILjava/lang/Object;)V from class org.apache.poi.openxml4j.opc.PackageRelationshipCollection

The missing jar files can be found here:
https://archive.apache.org/dist/poi/release/bin/poi-bin-3.13-20150929.zip

The missing jars are:
poi-ooxml
poi-ooxml-schemas

Might be good to update to the latest version of POI as well:
http://poi.apache.org/download.html

last_comment.author: Mridul Pathak
last_comment.text: I checked this on current trunk and it no longer happens. Uploading an .xlsx through the party profile Content upload reaches createDataResource without a mimeTypeId, and DataResourceWorker.getMimeTypeWithByteBuffer detects it as application/x-tika-ooxml without any error. The mismatch described here came from Tika's POI-based detector meeting a different POI version on the classpath. Trunk now uses a single POI version (OFBIZ-13731), and Tika 4 (OFBIZ-13719) no longer brings the parser bundles that contained that detector.

summary: Upgrade Checkstyle from 10.20.2 to 14.4.0
description:

Dependabot does not propose updates for this version string, so the pin is not tracked like the other build dependencies. The current release is 14.4.0.

Checkstyle 11 requires Java 17 and 13 requires Java 21. Trunk builds on Java 25 with Gradle 9.8.2, so both are met. The checks removed or changed between 11 and 14 (JavadocStyle, the WriteTag tagSeverity property, and the ImportOrder and Javadoc message wording) are not used in \{{config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml}}. Any new violations reported by the newer version will be fixed or, if a rule floods, suppressed narrowly in the configuration with a reason.

summary: Allow Dependabot major-version updates for Gradle dependencies on trunk
description:
The trunk gradle entry in {{.github/dependabot.yml}} ignores every major-version update ({{dependency-name: "*"}}, {{update-types: version-update:semver-major}}). The rule was added in April to let the minor and patch updates catch up, which they now have. It also freezes libraries that don't follow semver, such as owasp-java-html-sanitizer (date-based versions, about 2.5 years behind), icu4j and libphonenumber, and it hides real migrations such as Tomcat 11, Jersey 4, Spring 7, Groovy 6 and Gradle 9. This was proposed on dev@ with no objections: https://lists.apache.org/thread/wcmpxgy3sln77f9rgx0sw3jq29d6zonx

h3. Proposed change
* Remove the semver-major ignore from the trunk gradle entry.
* Add explicit ignores for deliberate pins so they don't keep coming back:
** {{org.asciidoctor.jvm.convert}} and {{org.asciidoctor.jvm.pdf}}: only the pdf plugin has a 5.x release, because 5.x renamed the convert plugin, so a lone pdf bump would split the pair.
** {{org.activiti:activiti-juel-jakarta}} {{>= 9}}: 9.0.0 is compiled for Java 25, and trunk targets Java 17.
* Leave the release24.09 gradle entry unchanged. Major upgrades don't belong on a release branch.

Each major-version PR is then triaged on its own. Routine ones go through the normal Dependabot review, real migrations are handled one at a time, and any we defer get an explicit ignore entry.

* The trunk gradle entry no longer ignores {{version-update:semver-major}}.

summary: Saving portlet attributes fails because setPortalPortletAttributes also stores request and servlet attributes
description:
The {{setPortalPortletAttributes}} event saves every entry of {{parameters}} as a {{PortletAttribute}}, but for Groovy events {{parameters}} is built with {{UtilHttp.getCombinedMap}}, which also holds the request, session and servlet-context attributes. Besides the submitted form fields it therefore tries to store entries such as {{org.apache.catalina.resources}}, and on trunk the 61-character {{org.apache.tomcat.util.net.secure_requested_protocol_versions}} overflows {{ATTR_NAME}} (60), so the save fails with an error and no portlet attribute is stored. release24.09 has the same code and builds {{parameters}} the same way.

h3. Fix
Store only the submitted request parameters ({{UtilHttp.getParameterMap(request)}}), still skipping the portal page and portlet keys, instead of iterating the combined {{parameters}} map.

summary: pricat import can pick up another user's running import thread, and its history never shows "importing"
description:
PricatParseExcelHtmlReport.initializeThread (and SampleHtmlReport.initializeThread) looks through the request thread's ThreadGroup and returns the first live PricatParseExcelHtmlThread it finds, whoever started it. prepareDisplayReport then calls start() on that thread, so an import started while another import is still running (including the 5 second wait at the end of run()) fails with IllegalThreadStateException instead of starting its own thread.

The ExcelImportHistory row is created in the PricatParseExcelHtmlThread constructor, before the thread is started, so isAlive() is always false and the row is stored as EXCEL_IMPORTED instead of EXCEL_IMPORTING. ExcelImportHistoryReport.ftl shows the in-progress state only for EXCEL_IMPORTING, so a running import shows no status at all.

summary: Groovy events that call success() or error() fail with GroovyCastException
description:
Since the Groovy DSL descriptor change ([#2096|https://github.com/apache/ofbiz-framework/pull/2096]), {{GroovyBaseScript.success(...)}} and {{error(...)}} are declared to return {{Map}}, but when the script runs as an event they return the String {{"success"}} or {{"error"}}, which Groovy cannot cast to {{Map}}. Every Groovy event that ends with {{success()}} or {{error()}} now throws a {{GroovyCastException}}: {{createInvoiceItemPayrol}} (accounting), {{duplicatePortalPage}} (common) and {{indexProducts}} (lucene). release24.09 still declares {{def}} and is not affected.

h3. Fix
Declare these methods with a return type that covers both the event String and the service Map again, and add a test that runs a Groovy event calling {{success()}} and {{error()}}.

summary: Upgrade the lucene plugin to Lucene 10
description: Lucene 10 requires Java 21, so the lucene plugin stayed on 9.12.3 while trunk was on Java 17. Lucene 10 removes {{IndexSearcher.doc}} and {{TopScoreDocCollector.create}}, which the content and product search scripts in the lucene and ecommerce plugins call, so a plain version bump would only fail at runtime. Upgrade to Lucene 10.6.0, switch the scripts to {{storedFields()}} and {{TopScoreDocCollectorManager}}, and remove the Dependabot ignore rule for Lucene 10.

summary: Move trunk to Java 25
description:
Raise trunk's Java source and target level from 17 to 25, the current LTS, before the release26.11 branch is created, as agreed on dev@ ("[PROPOSAL] Move trunk to Java 25 before the release26.11 branch"). release24.09 stays on Java 17.

The groundwork was done on Java 17 in OFBIZ-13732, OFBIZ-13743 and OFBIZ-13786, so trunk with the plugins already builds and passes all integration tests on JDK 25 at target 25 with only the version changed. The sub-tasks move the build, CI and images to Java 25, replace the Java 17 workarounds, and make the compiler lint fatal.

Once this lands, the dependency upgrades held back by Java 17 (Lucene 10, CAS LDAP support 7/8, activiti-juel-jakarta 9) can be taken in their own tickets.

summary: Make compiler lint warnings fatal

summary: Replace the Java 17 workarounds for Locale and Thread.getId
description: With target 25, javac reports 19 deprecation warnings, all from code kept compatible with Java 17: the {{Locale}} constructors and {{Thread.getId()}}. Replace them with {{Locale.of(...)}} and {{Thread.threadId()}} in the framework, applications and plugins, including the Groovy scripts that javac does not check, and remove the matching {{@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")}} annotations.

summary: Build, test and package trunk on Java 25
description:
Raise the source and target level in build.gradle from 17 to 25 and move everything that builds or runs trunk to JDK 25 in the same change, since a target 25 build fails on a JDK 17 runner:

* {{.github/workflows/gradle.yml}}: trunk matrix [17, 21] becomes [25]; release* branches stay [17].
* {{.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml}}: set up JDK 25 before the Gradle build (it uses the runner's default JDK 17 today).
* {{Dockerfile}}: {{eclipse-temurin:17}} becomes {{eclipse-temurin:25}} for the builder and runtime stages, pinned by digest.
* {{.devcontainer/devcontainer.json}}: {{java:17}} becomes {{java:25}}.
* {{README.md}} system requirements, the javadoc link to the Java SE API, and an Environment entry in {{UPGRADING.md}}.

summary: security.login.externalLoginKey.enabled is never checked by checkExternalLoginKey() and cannot be changed live
description:
ExternalLoginKeysManager.isExternalLoginKeyEnabled(request) (ExternalLoginKeysManager.java:241) caches the security.login.externalLoginKey.enabled property in a private static field on first read and never re-reads it. Any later change to the property -- via the properties file, or a live SystemProperty override through webtools (which normally takes effect immediately, no restart) -- has no effect on this class for the rest of the process's life; only a JVM restart picks it up.

Separately, checkExternalLoginKey(request, response) (ExternalLoginKeysManager.java:163) -- the consumption path wired into the default <preprocessor> chain used by the large majority of controller.xml files -- never calls isExternalLoginKeyEnabled() at all. The flag is only checked at the two key-generation call sites (RequestHandler.makeLink(), ScreenRenderer.java), never at redemption.

Net effect: an admin who disables security.login.externalLoginKey.enabled expecting the cross-app SSO mechanism to stop live gets no change in behavior, since the consumption path was never gated by the flag in the first place, and the flag itself can't be refreshed without a restart regardless.

Suggested fix:
- Re-read isExternalLoginKeyEnabled per call instead of caching it for the process's lifetime (or invalidate the cached field on a SystemProperty/property-cache change).
- Have checkExternalLoginKey() call isExternalLoginKeyEnabled(request) and short-circuit to "success" without consuming the key whe

summary: Missing permission checks on FinAccount GL-reconciliation services allow unauthorized reconciliation tampering
description:

summary: Add upgrade notes for the framework, applications and plugins
description:
OFBiz has no upgrade notes: the release notes only list JIRA issues, and applications/datamodel/DATAMODEL_CHANGES.adoc only covers application entities. Since release24.09, trunk has removed or changed a large number of public APIs, configuration options, components and plugins (75 pull requests now carry the api-change label), and upgraders need one place that tells them what to do.

This adds an UPGRADING.md for each layer, kept next to the code it describes so it moves with it when the framework and applications are separated: one at the framework root (environment, build, configuration, framework API, framework entities, themes), one in applications/ (application API, removed integrations), and one at the ofbiz-plugins root (a section per plugin, including removed plugins). Each has an "Upgrading to 26.11" section with Environment, Configuration, Code, Data and Removed subsections linking to the pull request or issue, and the README links to them. DATAMODEL_CHANGES.adoc stays the applications data-model file and gets the entity removals it is missing. The pull request template asks for an upgrade note whenever a change alters a public API.

summary: Remove the this-escape lint exclusion from the build
description:
Phases 1 and 2 (OFBIZ-13732, OFBIZ-13743) removed every this-escape warning, so trunk and the plugins now compile on JDK 25 with no this-escape or varargs warnings. This removes the {{-Xlint:-this-escape}} exclusion and its JDK-version check from build.gradle, so the JDK 21 CI build reports any new escape.

The 19 remaining deprecation warnings ({{new Locale(...)}}, {{Thread.getId()}}) need the Java 25 target ({{Locale.of}}, {{threadId()}}) and are left for the target upgrade, where the lint can also be made fatal with {{-Werror}}.

summary: Remove the remaining this-escape warnings and suppressed deprecations (phase 2, API changes)
description:
Phase 1 (OFBIZ-13732) removed every hidden or suppressed compiler warning that needed no API change. This phase removes the rest, which do need API changes. Each change is listed in its sub-task and in the release notes. Everything stays on Java 17 and lands on trunk only.

h3. API changes
* Classes that nothing subclasses become final or sealed: the widget models, the null entity sentinels, and ProductConfigWrapper's ConfigItem and ConfigOption. Their factories always create them with new, so a downstream subclass could never have been used.
* Protected methods with no callers become private or are removed: loadIncludes, FlexibleServletAccessor.init, getParentModel, TemporalExpression.setSequence and containsExpression.
* The public constructors of ModelEntity, ModelViewEntity, ModelGroupReader and the minilang operations are deprecated in favour of static factories. They are removed one release later, in phase 3.
* Security.setDelegator() and getDelegator() are replaced by a SecurityProvider SPI.
* A GenericDelegator subclass that bypasses DelegatorFactory must call the new initialization step.

h3. Entity and service engine safeguards
The entity and service engine sub-tasks land last, with one class or hierarchy per PR. Each one runs the full suite (cleanAll loadAll testIntegration with all plugins) on H2 and PostgreSQL, and its startup time is compared before and after. Each also gets a second committer review. Bugs found on these code paths are fixed in their o

last_comment.text:
h3. Public API changes in phase 2

Phase 2 removed or restricted the following public and protected API. Each class was checked for subclasses and callers in framework, applications, themes and plugins only, so a downstream project that extends or calls one of these will need to adapt. Please comment here if any of these affects you before the next major release.

h4. Classes made final, or whose constructors are no longer public
* {{ModelGrid}}, {{ModelSingleForm}}, {{ModelForm.FieldGroup}}, {{ModelForm.Banner}} are final; {{ModelForm.FieldGroupBase}} is sealed; the {{ModelForm}} constru

summary: Remove the hidden and suppressed compiler warnings (this-escape, varargs, dangling-doc-comments, deprecation)
description:
The build hides 84 this-escape and 5 varargs warnings through -Xlint exclusions, JDK 23+ reports 1,185 dangling-doc-comments warnings, and 24 @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") hide 30 calls to 13 deprecated APIs. This ticket removes all of them with design fixes, without new suppressions, so the build can run with -Xlint:all and no exclusions.

All of this work runs on Java 17. Each change is a sub-task with its own pull request.

h3. Phases
* Phase 1: changes with no API or behaviour change (sub-tasks below).
* Phase 2: changes that alter public API (final or sealed widget models, ModelEntity factories, GenericDelegator init step, SecurityProvider SPI). Notes for downstream projects go on this ticket and in the release notes.
* Phase 3: drop -Xlint:-this-escape and -Xlint:-varargs, make this-escape fatal on the JDK 21 CI job, remove the constructors deprecated in phase 2.

summary: Build ModelGroupReader through a static factory and add a public reload API
description: The constructor calls the overridable getGroupCache(), and devreload changes ModelGroupReader and ModelReader private fields by reflection. A factory loads the group cache fully before publishing the reader. A public reload() replaces the reflection, and devreload is updated in the same change. The public constructor is deprecated and will be removed in phase 3.

summary: devreload entity and entity-group hot-reload disabled since the readers lost their modelName field
description:
{{EntityModelReloader}} looks up the private {{modelName}} field of {{ModelReader}} and {{ModelGroupReader}} by reflection. That field was removed as unused on trunk, so the lookup fails and entity and entity-group hot-reload are disabled for the whole session, with an error in the log.

h3. Fix
Take the reader names from the keys of each reader cache instead of the removed field.

summary: ModelGroupReader publishes its entity-group map before it is filled
description:
{{ModelGroupReader.getGroupCache}} assigns an empty {{HashMap}} to the volatile {{groupCache}} field and then fills it, so a concurrent caller can read a half-built map, find no group for an entity and fall back to the delegator's default group, that is, the wrong datasource. On a stock instance this happens when an entitygroup resource fails to load at startup: the error is only logged, the reader is cached with a null map, and the next lookup rebuilds it on the shared instance while other requests read it.

h3. Fix
Build the map and the group-name set in local variables and publish them only once they are complete.

summary: Move GenericDelegator startup work into a Delegator lifecycle method
description:
The GenericDelegator constructor calls the overridable setDelegatorNames() and starts its other startup work. That work moves into a default lifecycle method on Delegator, which DelegatorConfigurable calls after construction. EntityCrypto is created on first use.

Release note: a GenericDelegator subclass that bypasses DelegatorFactory must call the new initialization method.

summary: Add static factories for ModelEntity and ModelViewEntity and deprecate their public constructors
description:
The ModelEntity and ModelViewEntity constructors call the overridable populateBasicInfo() and setEntityName(), and pass this to ModelField.create().

* New factories: createFromXml and createFromDatabaseMetaData on ModelEntity, createFromXml and createFromDynamicView on ModelViewEntity. They take an EntityAttributes value object, and the constructors only assign fields.
* The public constructors are deprecated and will be removed in phase 3.
* A committed snapshot test compares the old and new code paths for every entity and view entity: toXmlElement output, field order, primary keys, auto-stamp fields and relations.

summary: Make NullGenericEntity and NullGenericValue immutable sentinels
description: The GenericEntity NULL_VALUE sentinels call the overridable setImmutable() from their constructor. The sentinel classes become final and immutable from construction.

summary: performFind with a dynamicViewEntity fails on a tenant delegator
description: Since OFBIZ-12663, {{FindServices.prepareFind}} builds the model of a {{dynamicViewEntity}} with {{ModelReader.getModelReader(delegator.getDelegatorName())}}. For a tenant delegator the name is {{default#tenantId}}, which is not a delegator declared in entityengine.xml, so the lookup throws a {{GenericEntityConfException}} and {{performFind}}/{{performFindList}} return an error instead of searching. Using {{dynamicViewEntity.makeModelViewEntity(delegator)}} takes the reader from the delegator itself, which is what {{EntityQuery.from(dynamicViewEntity)}} already does in {{executeFind}}.

summary: Remove the this-escape warning in the ModelService copy constructor
description: The copy constructor calls the overridable addParamClone() for every parameter. The parameters are copied by a private helper into fields the constructor owns.

summary: Load the DispatchContext global service map with a static loader
description: The constructor calls the overridable getGlobalServiceMap(), which starts the loader tasks. A static loader builds the map from the delegator and the service configuration, and the constructor no longer calls an overridable method.

summary: ModelParam copy constructor drops nested attributes and shares the validator list
description:
The ModelParam copy constructor does not copy {{children}} and shares the original's {{validators}} list. Copied parameters (on the cloned services above) and parameters inherited through {{<implements>}} therefore lose the validation and type conversion of their nested attributes.

h3. Fix
Deep-copy the children and give the copy its own validators list.

summary: ModelService copy constructor shares the cached service's parameter map and drops required-permissions and notifications
description:
The ModelService copy constructor, which GenericDispatcherFactory uses for runSync, runSyncIgnore and runAsync with a transaction timeout or requireNewTransaction (every minilang call-service, Service ECA actions with new-transaction="true", form actions with ignore-error, RMI), assigns the cached service's {{contextInfo}} map to the copy and then puts the copy's cloned parameters into it. After one such call, the cached service's {{getParam()}} returns that call's clones, and concurrent calls write into the shared map without synchronization. The constructor also does not copy {{permissionGroups}}, {{notifications}} or the deprecation fields, so on these paths the service's required-permissions are not evaluated and its email notifications are not sent.

h3. Fix
Give the copy its own parameter map and copy the permission groups, notifications and deprecation fields.

summary: DispatchContext without a dispatcher caches an empty service map
description:
A {{DispatchContext}} created with a null dispatcher, as webtools {{LabelReferences}} and {{ArtifactInfoFactory}} do, loads the service definitions in tasks that each call {{getDelegator()}}, which dereferences the null dispatcher. Every task fails with a {{NullPointerException}}, {{ExecutionPool.getAllFutures}} logs and skips the failures, and the resulting empty map is cached under the entity model reader name (usually {{main}}).

h3. Impact
At startup the cache is already filled by the real dispatchers, so the problem stays hidden. After "Clear all caches" in webtools, if Artifact Info or the Label Manager is the first to load the service definitions, every dispatcher using that entity model reader fails with "Cannot locate service" until the caches are cleared again.

h3. Fix
Without a dispatcher, use the delegator configured for the named entity model reader to read the service definitions, and reject a name that no delegator uses instead of caching an empty map.

summary: Make the TemporalExpression sequence a final constructor argument
description:
Every TemporalExpression constructor calls the overridable setSequence(), and the Union, Intersection, Difference and Substitution constructors call containsExpression(this), which can never be true. The sequence becomes a final field set through super(). setSequence() and the dead containsExpression() check are removed.

Release note: TemporalExpression.setSequence() and containsExpression() are removed.

summary: Start the JmsListenerFactory loader thread only from the instance that wins
description: The constructor starts a thread that runs on this. The thread now starts in an explicit start() call, made only by the instance that wins the getInstance() compare-and-set.

summary: TemporalExpressionWorker overflows the stack on a cycle in TemporalExpressionAssoc
description:
{{TemporalExpressionWorker}} loads child expressions recursively through {{TemporalExpressionAssoc}} without tracking which expressions it is already loading. The {{createTemporalExpressionAssoc}} service does not prevent cycles (A to B to A, or A to itself), so loading such an expression for a persisted job or a calendar ends in a {{StackOverflowError}}.

h3. Fix
Track the expression ids on the current load path and throw an {{IllegalArgumentException}} naming the expression when a cycle is found. An expression shared by two parents is still allowed.

summary: TemporalExpression.compareTo drops members of a Union or Intersection that share a sequence
description:
{{TemporalExpression.compareTo}} returns 0 for two different expressions that have the same sequence value. Members are collected in a {{TreeSet}} (for example in {{TemporalExpressionWorker.getChildExpressions}}), so all but one of them are silently dropped. A UNION of two DATE_RANGE expressions (both sequence 800), or of two HOUR_RANGE expressions with the same start hour, ends up with a single member, and scheduled jobs and calendar entries miss dates without any error.

h3. Fix
Make {{compareTo}} a total order consistent with {{equals}}: order by sequence, return 0 only for equal expressions, then order by class name and by the fields of each expression type.

summary: JmsListenerFactory.getInstance starts a second loader thread when two dispatchers are created concurrently
description:
{{JmsListenerFactory.getInstance}} creates a new {{JmsListenerFactory}} and then publishes it with {{compareAndSet}}, but the constructor has already started the listener loader thread. When two {{ServiceDispatcher}} instances are created at the same time (webapps start in parallel), the instance that loses the race is discarded while its thread keeps running {{loadListeners}} over the same static listener and server maps.

h3. Effect
With a {{jms-service}} server configured with {{listen="true"}}, both threads can create and load a listener for the same server key, because each synchronizes on its own instance. Only one listener is kept in the map; the other stays connected, is never closed by {{closeListeners}} on shutdown, and on a topic every message runs the service twice. With the default configuration (no jms-service) the extra thread does one pass and exits.

h3. Fix
Start the loader thread only from {{getInstance}}, and only in the thread whose {{compareAndSet}} succeeds. The public constructor keeps its current behaviour.

summary: Remove the this-escape warning in the ShoppingCart copy constructor
description: The copy constructor calls the overridable getItemGroupByNumber() while it clones the item groups. A private lookup on the new cart's group map replaces it.

summary: Remove this-escape warnings in the pricat parser and report threads
description:
* The report is passed to AbstractReportThread and its subclasses through their constructors, instead of the overridable initHtmlReport() and setDelegator().
* AbstractReportThread overrides start() instead of calling setDaemon() in its constructor.
* The unused initBasicConds() call is removed.

This is the minimal fix. Redesigning the report threads around an executor and a registry will be a separate ticket.

summary: Remove this-escape warnings in ProductConfigWrapper and BOMTree
description:
* ProductConfigWrapper: ConfigItem and ConfigOption become final static nested classes that receive their context explicitly. The wrapper is built in a private helper instead of the overridable init().
* BOMTree and BOMNode: the tree no longer hands this to its root node. The value the node needs (rootAmount) is passed to print() instead.

summary: Copying a deserialized GenericValue fails with "observable cannot be null"
description:
GenericEntity keeps its Observable in a transient field, so it is null once the entity has been deserialized. GenericEntity.init(GenericEntity), used by GenericValue.create(GenericValue) and the copy constructors, and refreshFromValue both build the new Observable from that field directly, so copying or refreshing from a deserialized GenericValue throws an IllegalArgumentException ("observable cannot be null"). This breaks, for example, copying a shopping cart line restored from a persisted session.

h3. Proposed fix
Use the existing lazy getObservable() instead of reading the transient field in both places.

summary: ProductConfigWrapper fails with a NullPointerException after the session is restored
description:
ConfigItem.configItem is transient and never reloaded, so once a session holding a configured cart line is deserialized (Tomcat session persistence across a restart, or cluster replication), copying the line (ShoppingCartItem copy constructor, explodeItem) and calls such as isSingleChoice() or toString() throw a NullPointerException. ConfigOption.recalculateOptionPrice also uses the wrapper's transient delegator and dispatcher fields directly instead of getDelegator() and getDispatcher(), and it calls calculateProductPrice twice with the same arguments while checking only the second result for errors.

h3. Proposed fix
Reload configItem from configItemAssoc when it is null, use getDelegator() and getDispatcher() throughout, and drop the duplicate price call, checking the remaining result for errors.

summary: Build ArtifactInfoFactory through a static factory and link the artifact graph in populateAll()
description: The ArtifactInfoFactory constructor calls the overridable prepareAll(). The ControllerViewArtifactInfo constructor links itself into the artifact graph before it has been registered. The factory now constructs the object and then prepares it, and all linking moves into populateAll().

summary: Configurable product selections leak between shopping carts through the product config cache
description:
ProductConfigWorker.getProductConfigWrapper caches one ProductConfigWrapper per product, store, catalog, web site and currency, but on a cache miss it returns the cached instance itself, because {{putIfAbsentAndGet}} returns the value it stored. The caller then writes the customer's selections and comments into that instance and the cart item keeps it, so later visitors start from the first customer's choices (multi-choice questions are not reset) and later changes to that cart item change the cache.

Copies are not independent either: the ConfigOption copy constructor keeps the source option's parent ConfigItem and shares its {{componentOptions}} map. A copied cart line (ShoppingCartItem copy constructor, explodeItem) therefore computes isDefault and the offset prices against the source's selections, and a variant chosen on one copy changes the other.

h3. Proposed fix
Return a copy on a cache miss as well, attach copied options to the new ConfigItem, and copy the {{componentOptions}} map.

summary: Artifact Info graph loses or corrupts references when artifacts are loaded in parallel
description:
ArtifactInfoFactory.prepareAll() loads services and components on the global fork-join pool, but each {{get*ArtifactInfo}} method does a get, builds a new info, then a put on its map, so two tasks can build the same artifact and the later one replaces the earlier. The reverse-reference maps are filled with {{UtilMisc.addToSortedSetInMap}}, which does the same check-then-act and then adds to a plain {{TreeSet}} from many tasks at once, so a set can be replaced (losing the references already in it) or corrupted. The Artifact Info screens can also load artifacts on demand while another request iterates the same sets.

The fix registers each info with {{putIfAbsent}} and populates only the registered one, and keeps the reference sets in {{ConcurrentSkipListSet}}s created with {{computeIfAbsent}}.

summary: Add static factories for the minilang SimpleMapProcess, Copy and Convert operations and deprecate their public constructors
description: The SimpleMapProcess constructor calls the overridable readOperations(), and the Copy and Convert constructors call the overridable getFieldName() inherited from their parent. Each operation gets a static factory, and the field name is passed in as a value instead of being read from this. The public constructors are deprecated and will be removed in phase 3.

summary: Remove this-escape warnings in ConfigXMLReader, FlexibleServletAccessor and RecordIterator
description:
* ConfigXMLReader: loadIncludes() has no other callers and becomes private.
* FlexibleServletAccessor: the constructors assign the fields directly, and the unused protected init() becomes private.
* RecordIterator: the constructors open the stream through a private static helper.

Release note: two protected methods become private.
Depends on: bug tracker #11 (RecordIterator stream leak).

summary: FlexibleServletAccessor.hashCode throws a NullPointerException when the name is null
description:
FlexibleServletAccessor accepts a null name: the constructors treat it as an empty accessor, and equals compares null names safely. hashCode calls name.hashCode() without a null check, so it throws a NullPointerException for such an accessor, for example when it is put in a HashMap or HashSet. equals and hashCode are inconsistent: two accessors that compare equal cannot both be hashed.

h3. Proposed fix
Use Objects.hashCode(name) in hashCode.

summary: RecordIterator leaves the URL stream open when it cannot be created, and drops the cause
description:
When RecordIterator is created from a URL, it opens the stream and then reads the start of the file. If that fails, the constructor throws a DataFileException but never closes the stream it opened. It can fail on an unknown encoding, an IOException while skipping the configured start lines, or a first record that matches no record definition. The connection stays open until garbage collection. The "is not supported" and "Impossible to read the buffer" exceptions also drop the underlying exception, so the log doesn't show why the file couldn't be read.

h3. Proposed fix
In the URL constructor, close the stream and rethrow when the setup fails. Pass the original exception as the cause in both places.

summary: Make ModelTheme, ModelScreen, ModelMenu, ModelMenuItem and ModelTree final
description: These models build their children in their constructors and pass this to them as a back-reference. The renderers need that back-reference. The models are parsed once, shared between threads and always created with new by their own factories, so the classes become final. That makes passing this from the constructor safe, and javac no longer reports it. WidgetFactory and WidgetLoader, the supported extension points, are unaffected.

summary: Form fields inherited through form extends lose their ignore-when
description:
The ModelFormFieldBuilder copy constructors, the one taking a ModelFormField and the one taking another builder, copy every attribute except {{ignoreWhen}}. A field that a form inherits from its parent therefore loses its {{ignore-when}} condition.

h3. Proposed fix
Copy {{ignoreWhen}} in both copy constructors.

summary: Actions of a menu-item are never loaded
description:
ModelMenuItem looks for the {{actions}} element under the first child of {{condition}}, but widget-menu.xsd defines {{actions}} as a direct child of {{menu-item}}. As a result the actions of a menu-item are never read or run.

h3. Proposed fix
Read {{actions}} from the menu-item element.

summary: Menu items inherited through menu extends are renamed, so they can't be overridden or selected
description:
Since OFBIZ-12628, when a menu extends another one, each inherited menu item is copied with the child menu's name prefixed to the item name. A menu-item of the same name in the child menu is then added next to the inherited one instead of overriding it, and an inherited item never matches the selected item name, so it is never rendered as selected. For example, the "main" item of CommonAppBarMenu is never highlighted in the application bars that extend it, and SetupAppBar shows both the inherited main item and its own.

h3. Proposed fix
Keep the original item name when copying an inherited menu item. The copy still points to the child menu, which is what OFBIZ-12628 needed.

summary: Seal ModelForm to ModelGrid and ModelSingleForm and resolve the parent form before construction
description:
ModelForm calls the overridable getParentModel() from its constructor, and every FieldGroup it builds keeps a reference to the ModelForm under construction.

* ModelForm becomes sealed, permitting only ModelGrid and ModelSingleForm. A test first confirms that Mockito can still mock the class.
* A shared static resolver finds the parent form before super() is called. getParentModel() becomes private.
* FieldGroup keeps no reference to its form; its render methods receive the form as an argument.

summary: Field groups inherited through form extends still render with the parent form
description:
When a form extends another, ModelForm copies the parent's FieldGroup instances into its own field group list and map, and each FieldGroup keeps a reference to the form that created it. Rendering the child therefore opens the single-form wrapper with the parent's name and {{default-table-style}}, and FieldGroup.shouldUse decides whether to show a group from the parent's fields and {{use-when}} conditions, ignoring the child's overrides. No form shipped with OFBiz inherits a named {{field-group}} today, so in stock data the visible effect is limited to the wrapper of forms whose parent has a {{sort-order}}.

h3. Proposed fix
When inheriting from a parent, create a copy of each FieldGroup for the child form, keeping its id, style, title and collapsible flags, and point the inherited field names at the copies.

summary: Grid or form extending a missing parent in the same file fails with a NullPointerException
description:
ModelGrid.getParentModel and ModelSingleForm.getParentModel fall back to looking for a parent of the other widget type in the same file with {{findFirst().orElseGet(null)}}. When {{extends}} names something that is neither a grid nor a form in that file, {{orElseGet}} calls the null supplier and throws a NullPointerException, so the widget fails to load instead of logging "Failed to find parent ... definition" and continuing without a parent.

h3. Proposed fix
Use {{orElse(null)}} in both methods.

summary: Remove the unused HtmlMenuWrapper family, MenuWrapTransform and HtmlMenuRenderer
description: HtmlMenuWrapper, its subclasses and MenuWrapTransform have no callers. HtmlMenuWrapperImage throws an NPE in its constructor, and the wrapper looks up its classes in a package that was removed in 2015. Its constructor also calls the overridable init(). These classes are removed, along with HtmlMenuRenderer, which has no other users.

summary: Generate release notes with GitHub and label pull requests by type from their title prefix
description:
Release notes are currently generated from Jira, but only about half of the commits in a release carry an OFBIZ Jira ID, so many fixes are missing from the notes. As discussed on dev@, generate them with GitHub instead, leaving out Dependabot updates.

h3. Proposal
* Add {{.github/release.yml}} grouping pull requests into Bug fixes, Improvements, New features, Documentation and Other changes, excluding the {{dependencies}} label and {{dependabot[bot]}}.
* Add a workflow that sets the {{bug}}, {{enhancement}}, {{feature}} or {{documentation}} label of a pull request from its title prefix (Fixed, Improved, Implemented, Documented), with a manual mode to label pull requests already merged.

GitHub reads {{release.yml}} from the tag being released, so both files need to be on release24.09 before 24.09.09 is tagged.

OpenApiUtil.getAttributeSchema takes a Delegator argument. The method, its static field and the suppressions are removed.

summary: Start Java license headers with /* so javac no longer reports them as dangling doc comments
description: From JDK 23, javac reports a dangling-doc-comments warning when a /** comment is attached to no declaration. About 1,170 Java files start their license header with /*****, so javac reads it as a Javadoc comment; 142 files already use /*. This changes the first line of those headers to /* in a separate, script-generated commit, and moves or converts the 12 misplaced /** comments, mostly in secretshub.

summary: Remove this-escape warnings in OrderByList, ModelParam, MimeMessageWrapper, RecurrenceInfo and RecurrenceRule
description:
These constructors call their own overridable methods. Nothing subclasses these classes, so it is not a live bug, but -Xlint:-this-escape hides the warnings.

* ModelParam copy constructor: assign defaultValue directly instead of calling setDefaultValue().
* MimeMessageWrapper: constructors and public setters share private helpers.

summary: Remove this-escape warnings in ModelFormField, ModelFormFieldBuilder, HtmlWidget and the XmlWidget visitors

summary: Make entity condition lists and field maps immutable and remove the varargs lint exclusion
description:
EntityConditionListBase and EntityFieldMap keep a reference to the caller's array, list or map, although conditions are cached and used as cache keys. Generic varargs passed to Arrays.asList are also what raises the 5 varargs warnings hidden by -Xlint:-varargs.

summary: Integration tests fail on PostgreSQL because of duplicate GL account codes and row-order assumptions
description:
On PostgreSQL, 37 integration tests fail that pass on H2:
* {{InventoryIssuanceTestData.xml}} gives its four test GL accounts the codes 140000, 141000, 142000 and 500000, which the demo data already uses. PostgreSQL enforces the unique index {{GLACCT_UNQCD}}, so the data load fails and 35 {{inventoryissuancetests}} cases error out. H2 doesn't catch this because its datasources create unique indexes as non-unique.
* Once the data loads, {{testS3_4_ImpactPlanAudit}} fails because {{getProductionRunTaskForceIssueImpact}} loads the reallocation candidates without an order. When several reservations share one inventory item, which one gets reallocated depends on the order the database returns rows in.
* {{testDuplicateWorkEffortWithAssocsAndNotes}} reads the duplicated notes without an order and checks the first one, but the work effort has two notes at that point.

h3. Proposed fix
Give the test GL accounts unique codes. Order both reallocation-candidate queries by the reservation's {{createdStamp}}, so the oldest reservation is always reallocated first; this needs an explicit {{createdStamp}} alias in {{WorkEffortInvResAndItem}} and {{OrderItemShipGrpInvResAndItem}}, since {{alias-all}} never includes stamp fields. Check that the duplicated notes contain {{TestNote-1}} instead of relying on row order.

summary: Blob fields cannot be stored or read on PostgreSQL
description:
On PostgreSQL the {{blob}} field type is created as {{BYTEA}}, but {{BlobJdbcValueHandler}} uses {{PreparedStatement.setBlob}} and {{ResultSet.getBlob}}. The PostgreSQL JDBC driver maps those methods to large objects (OIDs), so storing a {{java.sql.Blob}} fails with "column ... is of type bytea but expression is of type bigint", and reading one fails with "Bad value for type long". This happens with both driver 42.2.24 and 42.7.2, and the {{entitytests}} testFieldTypes test fails on PostgreSQL because of it.

h3. Proposed fix
When the column's SQL type is binary ({{BYTEA}} maps to {{Types.BINARY}}), bind the blob with {{setBytes}} and read it back with {{getBytes}} wrapped in a {{SerialBlob}}. Other databases keep the current behaviour.

summary: getSystemInfoStatus counts completed communication event roles as open
description: The mini-lang counted the open communication events with an {{entity-count}} on {{CommunicationEventRole}}, where {{statusId}} is the role status. The Groovy counts the rows of the {{CommunicationEventAndRole}} view and filters them with {{statusId != 'COM_ROLE_COMPLETED'}}, but in that view {{statusId}} is the status of the CommunicationEvent and the role status is the {{roleStatusId}} alias (party-entitymodel.xml). The condition is therefore always true, completed role entries are counted as open, and the "Open communication events" figure is too high. Filter on {{roleStatusId}}.

The mini-lang {{<set>}} skipped a null source, so a missing content type kept the stored mimeTypeId; the Groovy stores null and {{store()}} wipes it (for example createContentFromUploadedFile derives the mimeTypeId from the file bytes and the attach step then erases it). summary: MacroFormRenderer refactoring
description:
Class MacroFormRender is 3400 lines long and performs the following:
 * Renders the various form structure parts and field widgets to FTL macros calls.
 * Configures the FTL environment.
 * Executes the FTL macro calls to generate HTML and write it to a caller provided Appendable.

Implementing the above means that MacroFormRenderer does not meet the Single Responsibility Principle. The current implementation of multiple responsibilities makes unit testing difficult.

As discussed on the dev mailing list https://markmail.org/message/adtkk6cb6o7mmy7f it is proposed that MacroFormRenderer is refactored.

Refactoring should separate the rendering of form structure parts and field widgets to FTL macro calls from the execution of those macros.

summary: Remove OFBizDynamicThresholdFilter and the ThreadContext "uri" entries that feed it
description:
h3. Problem
{{OFBizDynamicThresholdFilter}} (OFBIZ-11980) is declared as a configuration-wide filter in {{log4j2.xml}}, so it runs on every logging call, including the ones the logger levels then discard, only to keep {{/getJs}} requests at ERROR. summary: UtilXml position-tracking parse does not apply an entity-expansion limit
description:
The withPosition variant of UtilXml.readXmlDocument() (used when line/column
position tracking is requested) parses with a raw Xerces DOMParser. It sets the
external-entity features but, unlike the other UtilXml parsers, does not apply
an entity-expansion limit. The standard readXmlDocument() path obtains this
limit through FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on its DocumentBuilderFactory; the
position-tracking path has no equivalent, so a document with nested internal
entity definitions can expand without bound during parsing.

FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is not recognized by the raw Xerces DOMParser, and
disallowing DOCTYPE declarations is not an option on this path because it
validates documents that legitimately declare a DOCTYPE. The expansion limit
should instead be applied via the Xerces security manager
({{org.apache.xerces.util.SecurityManager}}), whose default entity-expansion
limit (100000) matches the limit already enforced on the standard path.

summary: UtilXml validating parse resolves external DTDs over the network when the DOCTYPE systemId is not available locally
description:
The default UtilXml.readXmlDocument() overloads parse in validating mode
({{validate=true}}). In validating mode the parser resolves the DTD declared by
a document's DOCTYPE, so it calls {{LocalResolver.resolveEntity()}}. When the
DTD cannot be resolved locally (not mapped in localdtds.properties and no
matching resource on the classpath), LocalResolver returns {{null}}:

{code:java}
Debug.logWarning("[UtilXml.LocalResolver.resolveEntity] could not find LOCAL DTD/Schema ...");
return null;
{code}

A null return lets the underlying parser fall back to resolving the systemId
itself, so a DOCTYPE whose systemId is a remote URL results in an outbound
network request to that URL during parsing. The {{load-external-dtd=false}}
feature does not cover this, because validation requires the DTD to be resolved.
The same applies to the second return path, {{return
defaultResolver.resolveEntity(...)}}, as the default handler also returns null.
External general entity resolution is already disabled, so document content is
not affected.

This leaves external DTD resolution enabled for every validating parse, which is
inconsistent with the external-entity hardening applied elsewhere in the
framework. The reachable call sites are limited (content-manager-authored
content, or the non-default allowZUGFeRDCompliantUpload option), so this is a
hardening improvement rather than a default-reachable defect.

Fix: have LocalResolver return an empty InputSource instead of nul

summary: cleanAll deletes the version-controlled package-lock.json files, making npm installs non-reproducible
description:
The {{cleanAll}} task depends on {{cleanNpmInstall}}, the Gradle {{clean<TaskName>}} rule for {{npmInstall}}. That rule deletes every output of {{npmInstall}}, which with {{npm install}} includes {{package-lock.json}}. As a result, {{./gradlew cleanAll loadAll}} removes the committed lockfiles (example, projectmgr, common-theme, and rest-api on trunk) and npm resolves all dependencies from scratch, so the build depends on whatever is published on the npm registry at that moment.

Since 2026-10-15 this breaks {{cleanAll loadAll}} on release24.09: vitest 5.0.5, reached through vite's optional peer {{@vitejs/devtools}}, makes npm 10.8.2 (bundled with Node 20.19.0) fail in {{:plugins:example:npmInstall}} with {{Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')}}. Trunk is not affected only because it uses Node 24 / npm 11.

h3. Fix
Make {{cleanNpm}} delete only {{node_modules}} and hook it into {{cleanAll}} (and rest-api's {{cleanDocAssets}} on trunk) instead of {{cleanNpmInstall}}, so the lockfiles are kept and installs stay reproducible.

summary: Survey PDF services read any server file named in the pdfFileNameIn parameter
description:
h3. Problem
{{PdfSurveyServices.getInputByteBuffer}} opens the free-text {{pdfFileNameIn}} parameter with {{new FileInputStream(pdfFileNameIn)}} and no path check, size limit or file-type check. The five survey PDF services that accept it ({{buildSurveyFromPdf}}, {{buildSurveyResponseFromPdf}}, {{getAcroFieldsFromPdf}}, {{setAcroFields}}, {{setAcroFieldsFromSurveyResponse}}) are {{auth="false"}} with no permission check. The {{buildSurveyFromPdf}} and {{buildSurveyResponseFromPdf}} requests are in the content controller, which is also included by ordermgr and partymgr, so any back-office user who can log in to one of those apps can make the server read a file of their choice.

h3. Impact
Form field names and values of any PDF form readable by the OFBiz process can be copied into survey records, bypassing {{content.data.local.file.allowed.paths}}. For other files the content is not returned, but the error message reveals whether the path exists (and its size on trunk). Pointing the parameter at a device or pipe makes the server read without limit or hang a request thread.

Remove the {{pdfFileNameIn}} parameter (service attributes, the {{getInputByteBuffer}} file branch, the BuildSurveyResponseFromPdf form field and its label) together with the unused {{pdfFileNameOut}} code. summary: Embedded H2 is never closed on shutdown, so committed data can be lost on restart
description:
Since H2 became the default database (OFBIZ-13412), the H2 URLs use {{DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE}} and nothing else closes the database, so every OFBiz exit, including {{ofbiz --shutdown}}, is an unclean close for H2. After such a close, H2's recovery can revert the database to an older state and silently drop committed data. On trunk, a row imported through webtools was gone after a normal restart, and once the whole database reverted to its schema-only state.

This affects trunk with the default embedded H2. release24.09 (Derby) and external databases are not affected. Fix: close the H2 datasources cleanly (close the pools or issue {{SHUTDOWN}}) at the end of shutdown, after all containers have stopped.

summary: Reject uploaded PDF files with hidden attachments or active actions
description:
h3. Problem
{{SecuredUpload.isValidPdfFile}} rejects PDF files containing JavaScript or embedded files, but the embedded-file check only reads the catalog's {{/Names /EmbeddedFiles}} tree. A file attached through a {{/FileAttachment}} annotation, or through any other file specification with an {{/EF}} entry, is not seen, so the PDF is accepted.

Other active PDF actions are not checked at all: {{/Launch}}, {{/ImportData}}, {{/GoToR}}, {{/GoToE}}, the multimedia actions and annotations ({{/Movie}}, {{/Sound}}, {{/Rendition}}, {{/RichMediaExecute}}, {{/RichMedia}}, {{/Screen}}), and {{/URI}} or {{/SubmitForm}} targets that are not http(s) (or mailto for {{/URI}}).

With the default {{allowZUGFeRDnotSecure=false}}, a PDF with a single valid ZUGFeRD/Factur-X attachment is always rejected. The check compares {{document.toString()}} with {{"[#document: null]"}}, and that is what every parsed DOM document returns.

h3. Fix
Use the same object-graph walk as the JavaScript check (every object reachable from the trailer, then every object in the cross-reference table) to:
* reject any file specification with an embedded file, except the single ZUGFeRD attachment in the names tree when {{allowZUGFeRDCompliantUpload}} is true
* reject the actions and annotations listed above, and {{/URI}} and {{/SubmitForm}} targets other than http/https (plus mailto for {{/URI}})
* reject the ZUGFeRD attachment only when no XML document can be read from it

trunk only; release24.09 is left

summary: ExampleJupiterTests.shouldExpirePreviousStatusOnCreateExampleStatus fails intermittently with a duplicate key on ExampleStatus
description:
h3. Problem
{{createExample}}'s return ECA calls {{createExampleStatus}}, which creates the first {{ExampleStatus}} row, and the test then immediately calls {{createExampleStatus}} again. Both rows use {{UtilDateTime.nowTimestamp()}} as {{statusDate}}, which is part of the {{ExampleStatus}} primary key ({{exampleId}}, {{statusDate}}). When both calls happen in the same millisecond, the second insert fails with a duplicate key error (H2 23505), so the test fails now and then in full {{testIntegration}} runs and passes when rerun.

h3. Fix
Make the test deterministic: before the second {{createExampleStatus}} call, wait until the current timestamp is later than the {{statusDate}} of the row created by the ECA. Leave the service unchanged. The collision only happens when two status changes are chained for the same example within one request, and {{statusDate}} is not a service input that the test could set itself.

Acceptance criteria: the test passes when the two calls would otherwise share a millisecond.

summary: Pass widget renderer values to the FreeMarker macros as data instead of building template text
description:
The screen, menu, tree and form renderers still build macro calls as strings such as {{<@renderLink id="..." text="..." />}} with the values pasted in and compile them as FreeMarker templates, so every value has to be escaped correctly as template code. {{FtlWriter}} already has the better pattern introduced in OFBIZ-11456 and its sub-tasks: the parameters are set in the FreeMarker environment and only a constant call to the macro is compiled with {{?with_args}}. This issue continues that work for all the renderers until the only template text that is compiled is one fixed call template and the string-building paths are removed.

The macro signatures of the theme libraries and the constructors of the {{Macro*Renderer}} classes are not changed. A few visible behaviours change because values are no longer interpreted as FreeMarker: a literal {{${...}}} in a value is printed as is, a null value is rendered as an empty string, HTML encoding of values is done in one place, and the tree renderer writes link images in the right position. Trunk only, no backport to release24.09.

Discussed on dev@ in the thread "[PROPOSAL] Widget renderers: pass values to the FreeMarker macros as data instead of building template text (continuing OFBIZ-11456)".

summary: Use a single Apache Shiro version and drop shiro-core
description:
h3. Problem
The build declares {{shiro-core}} 1.13.0 next to {{shiro-crypto-cipher}} 2.2.1, each with its own version ref, so Dependabot bumps them independently and the semver-major ignore rule keeps {{shiro-core}} on 1.x. At runtime 1.x modules (hash, cache, config, event) run against 2.x {{shiro-lang}}/{{shiro-crypto-core}}, and {{shiro-core}} 1.13.0 is a fat jar that duplicates some 2.x classes ({{org.apache.shiro.crypto.CryptoException}} among them), so which copy loads depends on classpath order.

{{EntityCrypto.getHashedKeyName}} relies on the 1.x {{DefaultHashService}} defaults (unsalted SHA-512, 1 iteration). In Shiro 2.x/3.x {{DefaultHashService}} defaults to argon2 with a random salt, so simply upgrading would make every {{EntityKeyStore}} lookup fail.

h3. Proposed change
* Compute the key-name hash explicitly as Base64(SHA-512(UTF-8 key name)) with the JDK, matching what is stored today.
* Remove {{shiro-core}} and depend only on {{shiro-crypto-cipher}}, {{shiro-crypto-core}} and {{shiro-lang}}, on one shared Shiro version (3.0.1).

Acceptance criteria: data and config values encrypted before the change still decrypt after it; full integration tests pass.

summary: GL-posting and order-completion invoicing commit-ECAs run with ambient userLogin instead of system
description:
*1. secas_ledger.xml GL-posting ECAs — no run-as-user*
{{createPayment}}/{{setPaymentStatus}} commit-ECAs call {{createAcctgTransAndEntriesForIncomingPayment}}/{{...ForOutgoingPayment}} with no {{run-as-user}}, so they inherit whichever caller's {{userLogin}} triggered the status change. These wrap {{createAcctgTransAndEntries}}, which requires the {{ACCTG_ATX}} permission, so a caller without it would fail the GL posting and roll back the whole transaction.

*2. createInvoiceFromOrder ECA — partially-billed branch not elevated*
The sibling "nothing billed yet" branch ({{createInvoiceForOrderAllItems}}) already substitutes the {{system}} userLogin before invoicing, with a comment noting this is required. The "partially billed" branch in {{InvoiceServicesScript.groovy}} skips that step, inherits the ambient userLogin, auto-approves to {{INVOICE_READY}}, and cascades into {{capturePaymentsByInvoice}} → {{createPayment}}, hitting the same permission check.

Planned fix: add {{run-as-user="system"}} to the affected ECAs in {{secas_ledger.xml}} and {{secas.xml}}, and align the groovy branch with its sibling.

summary: Create a guide to help users set up a perishable goods business in Apache OFBiz using AI tools of their choice.
description:
We intend to create a guide that helps users set up a perishable goods business in Apache OFBiz without any manual data entry. The idea is that the user will describe their business in plain language, and the AI will write the complete Apache OFBiz data file for them. They'll review the setup it generates, import the file, and their core perishable goods data will be loaded into Apache OFBiz. No Apache OFBiz expertise and no manual XML work required.
The guide will cover perishable goods such as juice, dairy, bread, produce, and frozen products, which need clear storage rules and batch-level expiry tracking. Apache OFBiz will hold all of this, along with the product, inventory, supplier, warehouse, and replenishment data needed to run the business.

It will walk the user through five steps: answer a few questions about the business, download the prompt file from the page, send both to the AI of their choice, check what it generates, and import it into Apache OFBiz. In a few minutes, they'll be able to load the core setup without creating a single Apache OFBiz record by hand.

The guide will be published to Confluence as a reference.

summary: Promo conditions PPIP_ORST_YEAR and PPIP_ORST_LAST_YEAR read the order sub-total from the wrong map
description:
{{productOrderYear}} ("Order sub-total X since beginning of year", PPIP_ORST_YEAR) and {{productOrderLastYear}} ("Order sub-total X since beginning of last year", PPIP_ORST_LAST_YEAR) in {{ProductPromoCondServices.groovy}} call {{getOrderedSummaryInformation}} and keep its answer in {{serviceResult}}, but then read the total with {{result.get('totalSubRemainingAmount')}}. {{result}} is the condition's own {{success()}} map, so the sub-total is always null and the condition is compared as if the customer had ordered nothing, whatever the order history is. {{productOrderHist}} (PPIP_ORST_HIST) reads {{serviceResult}} correctly and is not affected.

summary: Support for replenishment of a secondary warehouse from a main warehouse
description:
At the onset let me define a few terms clearly as I mean it in the story description below :
Requirement - A request generated for a particular product for a specific quantity that needs to be purchased from a supplier for satisfying certain inventory needs of a particular facility.
Replenishment - A request generated for a particular product for a specific quantity that needs to be transferred from a "backup facility" for satisfying certain inventory needs of a particular facility.
Fulfilment - The process of reserving, picking, packing and shipping the ordered quantity of product(s) as per a sales order.
Terms 'warehouse' and 'facility' have been used interchangeably.

*The Use Case:*

Consider a scenario wherein there is a website and a physical retail store of the same Company.
Each having its own facility i.e. 1:1 mapping.

There is a Requirement Method Enum ID (RMEI) of each product which is applicable irrespective of the store and supersedes the RMEI defined, if any, on a store.

description:
Two update() DSL calls pass two arguments to EntityUpdateBuilder.where(), which only accepts a Map.

*1. {{resetEntitySyncStatus()}}*
{{update('EntitySync').where('entitySyncId', parameters.entitySyncId)}} throws {{MissingMethodException}}, since {{EntityUpdateBuilder}} has only {{where(Map)}}. *2. {{setTimeZoneFromBrowser()}}*

summary: Make MultiTrustManager reject untrusted certificates when its all-trusted properties are missing or empty
description:
MultiTrustManager validates certificates against the configured trust anchors, but when the validation fails it ignores the failure if the property server.all-trusted (outgoing connections) or client.all-trusted (client certificates) of certificate.properties is "true". The code reads both properties with the default "true", so a certificate.properties without these entries, or with an empty value, silently disables the certificate validation. The shipped file sets both to false, so a default installation is not affected.

h3. Proposed change

Read both properties with the default "false", so that a missing or empty value keeps the validation on and only an explicit "true" disables it.

summary: Strip control characters from the Location header set by RequestHandler.callRedirect and by the SEO forward filters
description:
RequestHandler.callRedirect sets the Location header from a URL that can contain values taken from the request: the decoded path info and query string in the redirect to the secure channel, and the saved previous request (_PREVIOUS_REQUEST_, the decoded path info) used after a login. A decoded path can contain carriage return and line feed characters, which should never end up in a response header. Tomcat replaces control characters when it writes the header, so this is not exploitable today, but the application should not rely on the container for it. The same applies to SeoContextFilter.forwardUri and UrlRegexpTransform.forwardUri, which set Location from the request URI (only when SEO URL regular expressions are configured).

h3. Proposed change

Strip control characters from the URL before setting the Location header, in one shared place used by RequestHandler.callRedirect and by the two SEO filters, as already done for the CMS alias redirect in OFBIZ-13645.

summary: Escape backslash and braces in the FreeMarker macro strings built by the macro menu, tree and form renderers
description:
MacroMenuRenderer.executeMacro(Appendable, String, Map), MacroTreeRenderer (imgStr) and MacroFormRenderer (encodeDoubleQuotes) build parts of a macro call as template text and only escape the double quote of the value. Backslashes and the FreeMarker interpolation characters are left as they are, so a value containing them is interpreted by FreeMarker instead of being rendered literally (or fails to parse). MacroScreenRenderer.executeMacro already escapes backslash, double quote and the opening brace.

h3. Proposed change

Add one shared helper that escapes a value for a double-quoted FreeMarker string literal (backslash, double quote, opening brace), use it in MacroScreenRenderer and in the three places above in place of the quote-only escaping, and add unit tests that render values containing backslashes, quotes, ${...}, #{...} and braces and check that they come back literally. Existing widget output must stay the same for normal text.

h3. Scope and risk

Only the existing quote-only escapes are replaced. *Why accounting quantity?*

When inventory is shipped, there's an accounting transaction that debits the inventory on hand value and credits Cost of Goods Sold (COGS). 

There's more than one way of deciding what value is added to COGS. 

First and most obvious is the actual cost of the inventory item. But companies may prefer other strategies. summary: SafeObjectInputStream allowList matches class names as substrings and ships with unescaped dots
description:
h3. Problem
{{SafeObjectInputStream.resolveClass()}} checks a class name against the allowList with {{Matcher.find()}}, which accepts any name that merely *contains* an allowed fragment. The allowList shipped in {{framework/base/config/SafeObjectInputStream.properties}} also overrides the stricter built-in defaults, uses unescaped dots ({{java..*}}, {{org.apache.ofbiz..*}}) and still contains the test-only entries {{foo}} and {{SerializationInjector}}.

h3. Impact
In practice any class whose name contains {{java}} followed by a character (e.g. {{javax.*}}, {{javassist.*}}) or the text {{foo}} is accepted, instead of only {{java.*}} and {{org.apache.ofbiz.*}}. The filter therefore admits much more than intended. This is defense-in-depth hardening: exploiting it still requires attacker-controlled serialized data to reach a deserialization point, and none is known to be reachable unauthenticated in a default deployment (the SOAP endpoint is disabled, OFBIZ-12212).

h3. Fix
* Require the whole class name to match an allowList entry ({{Matcher.matches()}}); object-array names such as {{[Ljava.lang.String;}} are matched on their element type so arrays of allowed classes keep working.
* Escape the dots in the shipped allowList and remove the test-only entries (the tests set their own allowList).

Deployments that add custom classes to allowList should make sure each entry matches the full class name, e.g. {{mycompany\\.foo\\..*}}.

summary: Resolve component: locations with ComponentLocationResolver in CommonEvents.openSourceFile and make ComponentConfig.getComponentConfig(String) lookup-only
description:
Related to CodeQL alerts 1810, 1543 and 1811. Two small changes are proposed to make the code say what it already does.

h3. 1. CommonEvents.openSourceFile

The method only accepts locations that start with {{component:}}, but resolves them through {{FlexibleLocation}}, which accepts every location type. Proposal: resolve them with {{ComponentLocationResolver}} directly.

h3. 2. ComponentConfig.getComponentConfig(String)

The single-argument overload delegates to the two-argument one with a null root location, which can only return a cached config or throw. Proposal: make it an explicit lookup-only method and use it in {{getFullLocation}}. The existing TODO on this method suggests lazy loading of components by name; that does not seem needed, since all components are loaded at startup, so the comment would be removed. The intent is no change in behavior.

h3. Release branch

release24.09 has the same code and the same alerts. A backport is planned once the change on trunk shows the alerts clearing.

summary: setCommEventRoleToRead and setCommunicationEventRoleStatus NPE when no role exists
description:
Both methods look up a {{CommunicationEventRole}} that can legitimately be absent (no matching role for the given party/event), then unconditionally dereference the result:
{code:groovy}
eventRole = from('CommunicationEventRole').where(...).queryFirst()
parameters.roleTypeId = eventRole.roleTypeId  // NPE if eventRole is null
{code}
The original minilang's field access is null-safe, so a missing role was silently a no-op. Both services are auth-callable and reachable whenever a caller checks status/marks-read for a party that isn't a role participant on the event.

Needs fixing: null-guard {{eventRole}}/{{communicationEventRole}} in both methods before dereferencing, matching the original's graceful no-op.

summary: Six regressions in the minilang-to-Groovy conversion of ProductServicesScript.groovy, including a guaranteed crash and a permission-scope gap
description:
*1. {{deleteProductGroupOrder()}} always throws — CRITICAL*
{{productGroupOrder.removeRelated('OrderItemGroupOrder')}} — no such relation exists on {{ProductGroupOrder}}'s entity model, so this throws every time. The parent is also removed before its children, which would violate the FK even if the relation name were fixed. Needs reordering plus a correct child-removal query.

*2. {{checkProductRelatedPermission()}} drops a date filter — security-relevant*
{{.filterByDate('roleFromDate', 'roleThruDate')}} replaces rather than adds to the default filter pair, so the product's own category-membership window is never checked — only the party's role-assignment window is. A limited-admin can retain edit/delete rights on a product whose category membership has expired. Fix: pass both pairs in one call.

*3-4. Added {{.cache()}} not in the original mini-lang*
{{forceIndexProductKeywords()}} and {{deleteProductKeywords()}}'s {{Product}} lookups now cache; the force-reindex method in particular can read stale data.

*5. Groovy truthiness on {{cancelQuantity}}*
{{orderItem.cancelQuantity ?: orderItem.quantity}} wrongly falls back when {{cancelQuantity}} is legitimately 0.

*6. Wrong string in {{updateProductQuickAdminName()}}*
Passes {{'updateQuickAdminName'}} instead of {{'updateProductQuickAdminName'}} — cosmetic, wrong text in a permission-denied message.

summary: HashCrypt compares non-PBKDF2 password hashes with variable-time String.equals()
description:
{{HashCrypt.doComparePbkdf2()}} compares password hashes in constant time, but the other three comparison helpers ({{doCompareTypePrefix()}}, {{doComparePosix()}}, {{doCompareBare()}}) use {{String.equals()}}. That call returns at the first character that differs (CWE-208). {{doComparePosix()}} handles the default {{password.encrypt.hash.type=SHA}} format, so this path runs on every stock login.

Proposed fix: replace {{String.equals()}} with {{MessageDigest.isEqual()}} in all three helpers, so that every comparison path uses the same constant-time discipline as PBKDF2. The result for any input stays the same.
