summary: EntityCrypto uses AES in ECB mode for encrypt="true" fields, producing deterministic ciphertext
description:
h3. Problem

{{EntityCrypto}}'s {{ShiroStorageHandler}} explicitly configures its AES cipher with
{{cipherService.setMode(OperationMode.ECB)}} for the {{EncryptMethod.TRUE}} case, used by
every entity field with {{encrypt="true"}} in entitydef XML. ECB mode has no initialization
vector and is deterministic: identical plaintext under the same key always produces
identical ciphertext. The {{EncryptMethod.SALT}} path ({{encrypt="salt"}}) does not override
the cipher mode and gets Shiro's own default (GCM, authenticated encryption with a random
nonce) for free -- but {{encrypt="salt"}} is currently used only in the test entity model,
never by a real entity, so effectively every encrypted field in production goes through the
weaker ECB path.

h3. Proposed fix

* Remove the explicit {{setMode(OperationMode.ECB)}} override so {{EncryptMethod.TRUE}}
  falls through to the same safe default already used by {{SALT}}.
* Retire {{encrypt="salt"}} as a separate option now that it is redundant with
  {{encrypt="true"}}; update {{entitymodel_test.xml}} accordingly.
* {{decryptValue}} needs to keep decrypting legacy ECB-encrypted values as a fallback until
  they are migrated, mirroring the existing 3-DES fallback retained since the 2015 AES
  rewrite.
* Fix the existing {{reencryptFields}} service (see OFBIZ-6694) so it can serve as the
  migration path -- it currently selects only the target field and omits the primary key,
  causing {{store()}} to fail after re-encr

summary: PBKDF2 password verification always fails in HashCrypt.doComparePbkdf2
description:
When {{password.encrypt.hash.type}} is set to any of the documented PBKDF2 options ({{PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1/256/384/512}}), no user can log in, even with the correct password.

{{HashCrypt.doComparePbkdf2}} wraps the decoded salt in {{Arrays.toString(...)}} before using it, so the salt used for verification never matches the one used to create the hash. This was introduced in OFBIZ-11142 (commit 2c2340db0a, 2019) during the move to {{java.util.Base64}}. The default {{SHA}} hash type is not affected.

The fix is to use the decoded salt bytes directly. Hash creation is unchanged, so existing PBKDF2 hashes work again after the fix, both those created since 2019 and older ones (e.g. the demo examples in {{PasswordSecurityDemoData.xml}}). No migration is needed.

summary: removeImageBySize() silently swallows a failed sub-service call inside a .each closure
description:
h3. Needs fixing

{{applications/product/src/main/groovy/org/apache/ofbiz/product/product/imagemanagement/ImageManagementServicesScript.groovy}}'s {{removeImageBySize()}} has {{return error(serviceResult.errorMessage)}} inside a {{contentAssocs.each { GenericValue contentAssoc -> ... } }} closure, guarding the result of {{removeProductContentForImageManagement}}. Since {{return}} inside a Groovy closure only exits that closure invocation, a failure here does not abort {{removeImageBySize()}} — the method just moves on and eventually returns {{success()}} regardless. The original minilang-to-Groovy conversion used a plain {{for}} loop here (correct); a later, purely stylistic "Codenarc integration rebased" commit converted it to {{.each { }}} with no other logic change, introducing this bug. Needs fixing: convert the {{.each}} loop back to a plain {{for}} loop so a failed {{removeProductContentForImageManagement}} call correctly aborts {{removeImageBySize()}} with an error.

Also present on release24.09, at the same path, in the identical form.

Acceptance criteria: fixed, with a regression test that forces {{removeProductContentForImageManagement}} to fail and asserts {{removeImageBySize()}} returns an error rather than silently succeeding.

summary: calculateShoppingListDeepTotalPrice() silently drops failed price/subtotal
description:
h3. Needs fixing

{{applications/order/src/main/groovy/org/apache/ofbiz/order/shoppinglist/ShoppingListServicesScript.groovy}}'s {{calculateShoppingListDeepTotalPrice()}} has {{return error(...)}} inside two separate {{.each { }}} loops: once when {{calculateProductPrice}} fails for a shopping list item, and once when the recursive {{calculateShoppingListDeepTotalPrice}} call fails for a child shopping list. In both cases, {{return}} only exits that closure invocation, not the enclosing method, so the failure is silently absorbed — the loop simply moves on to the next item/child list without adding anything for the failed one, and the method returns a *plausible-looking but understated* {{totalPrice}} instead of an error. This is worse than a crash: the caller has no way to know the total is wrong. Needs fixing: convert both {{.each}} loops back to plain {{for}} loops so a failure correctly aborts {{calculateShoppingListDeepTotalPrice()}} with an error instead of silently producing a wrong total.

Also present on release24.09, at the same path, in the identical form (both {{.each}} call sites).

Acceptance criteria: fixed, with a regression test that forces one of the two failure paths and asserts the service returns an error rather than a silently-understated total.

summary: Add support for multiple, independent REST-APIS in one OFBIz instance
description:
In more complex project scenarios, it can be necessary to host more than one independent REST API with different credentials, authorization rules, and security groups.

Typical examples include connecting different applications or external integrations, where each integration should have its own API boundary and security configuration.

Each independent REST API should have:

Its own API group and routing context.
Its own configurable authorization/security groups.
A separate verification/authentication endpoint, where required.
Its own OpenAPI specification containing only the endpoints belonging to that API.
Its own Swagger UI displaying only the endpoints belonging to that API.
A clearly distinguishable URL structure.
Proposal

The REST API plugin in its current form is well suited for this improvement. A first implementation plan looks roughly as follows.

1. Introduce apiGroup in rest.xml

Add a new apiGroup parameter at the <api> level in rest.xml.

The apiGroup parameter defines the logical API to which the REST endpoints belong and effectively replaces the current <api>-level path as the mechanism for separating API groups.

For backwards compatibility, <api> definitions that do not explicitly declare an apiGroup should be assigned a default group, for example:

api

summary: Open combined PDF in browser from Find Orders View (PDF) action
description:
*Current behavior*

On Find Orders (ordermgr), the mass actions for PDF output are "Print (PDF)", which
sends one print job per selected order to a printer, and "Create File", which writes
one PDF per selected order on the server under \{{runtime/output/}}. There is no way
to view the PDFs of the selected orders in the browser.

*Improvement*

Add a new "View PDF" action to the Find Orders mass action dropdown that opens one
combined PDF containing all selected orders in a new browser tab. The existing
"Print (PDF)" and "Create File" actions remain unchanged.

*Proposed fix*

# Add a request-map \{{orders.pdf}} in the ordermgr controller, backed by a Java event
  that loops the selected orderIdList, renders the existing
  \{{OrderPrintScreens.xml#OrderPDF}} screen per order through the existing
  ScreenRenderer + FOP pipeline, merges the results with PDFBox \{{PDFMergerUtility}}
  (already an OFBiz dependency), and streams the combined PDF inline as
  \{{application/pdf}}.
# Add a "View PDF" option to the mass action dropdown in \{{FindOrders.ftl}}, opening
  the PDF in a new browser tab.
# Add a new \{{OrderViewOrdersPdf}} label.

summary: updateContentPermission grants UPDATE via ancestor ownership without an ownership-change request
description:
In {{updateContentPermission}}, the ownership parent-walk block (the {{while}} loop checking ancestor ownership) is nested as a sibling of the {{ownerContentId}} check instead of inside it. In the original minilang, the parent-walk was only reachable when {{ownerContentId}} was supplied, differed from the content's current owner, and a second ownership check also failed — i.e., only during an explicit ownership reassignment. As converted, the parent-walk instead fires whenever the direct ownership check on {{contentId}} fails, regardless of whether {{ownerContentId}} was ever supplied. A user who doesn't own a piece of content directly, and isn't requesting any ownership change, is now granted UPDATE permission if they own any ancestor in its ownership chain.

Needs fixing: re-nest the ancestor parent-walk block inside the {{ownerContentId}}-supplied branch, matching the original minilang's condition structure.

summary: Harden testServiceDeadLockRetry to remove timing-dependent Thread.sleep in service engine tests
description:
The service engine's deadlock-retry test (testServiceDeadLockRetryThreadA / ThreadB in ServiceEngineTestServices.java) relies on a fixed Thread.sleep(100) to make two concurrent threads race into a circular-wait deadlock. This is inherently timing-dependent: it worked reliably against the database timings this test suite has historically run under, but a database version change (encountered while evaluating a H2 database upgrade) shifted internal timings enough that the two threads no longer reliably collided, causing service-dead-lock-retry-assert-data to fail intermittently.

This ticket hardens the test to use real thread synchronization instead of a sleep, so the deadlock is triggered deterministically regardless of the underlying database's timing.

h3. Root cause detail

Each thread now signals a {{CountDownLatch(1)}} once it holds its own lock, then waits on the other thread's latch before attempting the second lock, guaranteeing the circular wait instead of guessing at timing.

A latch is required rather than a barrier-style rendezvous: {{ServiceDispatcher.runSync}}'s own deadlock-retry loop retries only the losing thread's service call in isolation after a real deadlock, not both threads together. summary: Add real POI-based .xlsx export via a new screenxlsx view-handler type
description:
h3. Problem

The {{screenxls}} view-handler type ({{MacroScreenViewHandler}}, driven by {{XlsFormMacroLibrary.ftl}}/{{XlsScreenMacroLibrary.ftl}} under {{themes/common-theme}}) claims a content-type of {{application/vnd.ms-excel}} but never produces a real binary workbook - the macros only emit plain HTML {{<table>}} markup. Excel opens this leniently (with a "file format doesn't match extension" warning), but other tools (LibreOffice, Google Sheets import, etc.) are far less forgiving. Apache POI ({{org.apache.poi:poi}}) is already a framework dependency, but only used for spreadsheet *import* today ({{ImportProductServices.java}}) - there's no export usage to build on.

h3. Proposal

Add a new {{screenxlsx}} view-handler type (content-type {{application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet}}) that produces a genuine binary {{.xlsx}} workbook via Apache POI. Since a real {{.xlsx}} is a binary format, this needs a different rendering approach than the FreeMarker-macro pipeline {{screenxls}}/{{screencsv}}/{{screen}} share - likely a new {{AbstractViewHandler}} implementation (see {{ScreenFopViewHandler}} for how PDF output handles a non-macro rendering path) paired with a {{FormStringRenderer}} implementation that writes POI cells directly instead of macro-call text.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* New {{screenxlsx}} view-handler type registered in {{handlers-controller.xml}}
* Produces a real, valid OOXML {{.xlsx}} binary - opens cleanly in Excel and L

summary: Fix Mini-lang to Groovy regressions in InvoiceServicesScript.groovy
description:
During the conversion of InvoiceServices.xml from Mini-lang to Groovy (OFBIZ-13085), several logic regressions, inverted filters, desynchronized calculations, and unhandled null dereferences were introduced:

1. getInvoicesFilterByAssocType:
In Mini-lang, <if-empty field="invoiceItemAssocList"> added the invoice to filteredInvoiceList so that only invoices without an association of the given type were returned. In Groovy, this condition was inverted to "parameters.invoiceList.findAll\{ invoiceIds.contains(it.invoiceId) }", returning only invoices that already have the association. This breaks the Commission Run feature by repeatedly reprocessing already-commissioned invoices and ignoring uncommissioned invoices.

2. addTaxOnInvoice:

summary: Support for Inventory Cycle Count Data Model and Services
description:
*Summary*
As discussed on the mailing list, this ticket is to introduce basic support for the Inventory Cycle Count feature in Apache OFBiz. This is the first phase to establish the core data model and service layer.
 
*Objectives*
- Data Model: Define entities for InventoryCount, Items, Variance, and Status history.
- Seed Data: Add standard statuses (In-Progress, Completed, Cancelled) and transitions.
- Security: Implement permissions for VIEW, CREATE, UPDATE, and ADMIN operations.
- Services: Implement basic CRUD services using the entity-auto engine.
 
*Goal*
Provide a standardized way to orchestrate physical inventory counts and record variances without disrupting warehouse operations.

summary: Inventory Cycle Count
description: System-guided Inventory Cycle Count capability for Apache OFBiz® Inventory Management. Many warehouse operations running Apache OFBiz still fall back on manual, spreadsheet-based inventory counts because the application has no built-in way to direct, track, and reconcile a count without pausing normal warehouse activity. This capability closes that gap: a Supervisor creates a Cycle Count by selecting SKU to verify (by Inventory Item, Location, LPN, or a combination, or via CSV import); a Worker counts each resulting Count Item individually; and any variance from the expected system quantity is routed to the Supervisor for review before inventory records change. The goal is to eliminate the inaccuracies introduced by manual counting, keep counting running alongside normal warehouse activity without disruption, and maintain a complete, auditable record of every count and adjustment.

summary: Fix Mini-lang to Groovy regressions in InvoiceServicesScript.groovy
description:
During the conversion of InvoiceServices.xml from Mini-lang to Groovy (OFBIZ-13085), several logic regressions were introduced in InvoiceServicesScript.groovy:

1. isInvoiceInForeignCurrency:
   - Inverted boolean: returns true when currency equals base currency, and false when different.
   - Accesses serviceResult.baseCurrencyUomId directly instead of serviceResult.partyAccountingPreference?.baseCurrencyUomId, always resolving to null.

2. setInvoiceStatus:
   - invoice.paidDate is assigned unconditionally outside the INVOICE_PAID check, setting paidDate on any status transition (e.g. INVOICE_APPROVED, INVOICE_SENT).

3. updateInvoice:
   - Multiple typos using statustId instead of statusId, resulting in missing statusId in label parameters, failure to mask statusId during setNonPKFields, and passing null statusId to setInvoiceStatus.

4. createInvoiceItem & updateInvoiceItem:
   - Product lookup uses where(parameters) instead of where(productId: ...), attempting to match non-Product entity fields like invoiceId.
   - createInvoiceItem uses if (!invoiceItem.amount), which treats 0 as falsy and recalculates price when amount is 0.

5. cancelInvoice:
   - Assumes any non-receipt payment is a disbursement (setting PMNT_SENT) rather than checking isDisbursement, and lacks null-safety when querying related Payment.

summary: javadoc task fails when docs.groovy-lang.org is unreachable
description:
h3. Problem
The {{javadoc}} task links to Groovy's API docs via {{options.links(...)}}, which fetches an {{element-list}} from {{docs.groovy-lang.org}} over the network at build time. That site is frequently unreachable, and since {{failOnError = true}}, a connection timeout fails the whole task. This has been failing trunk, release24.09, and PR builds on both GitHub Actions and BuildBot with:
{code}
error: Error fetching URL: https://docs.groovy-lang.org/docs/groovy-4.0.22/html/api/ (java.net.ConnectException: Connection timed out)
{code}
The link also pointed at Groovy 4.0.22, stale against the actual {{groovy-all}} 5.1.1 dependency.

h3. Fix
Switch to {{-linkoffline}}: generated links still point at the real {{docs.groovy-lang.org}} site, but the required {{element-list}} is read from a local copy instead of fetched live. That copy is extracted at build time from Groovy's own javadoc jar, resolved from Maven Central using the same version already declared for the groovy-all dependency, so it tracks future Groovy version bumps automatically with nothing to hand-maintain.

A candidate fix along these lines has been tested locally, confirming the task completes without depending on docs.groovy-lang.org at build time even while the site was down; PR to follow.

To be backported to release24.09, which has the same issue against an older Groovy version.

summary: Replace flaky fixed Thread.sleep(3000) in LuceneTests with a bounded polling loop
description:
LuceneTests.groovy sleeps a fixed 3 seconds after calling indexContentTree, before searching the Lucene index, to let indexing finish. indexContentTree only enqueues documents onto a background thread's queue and returns immediately — the actual IndexWriter write/commit/close happens asynchronously with no join(), future, or other hook to synchronize on. A fixed sleep is therefore both racy (can fail under slow CI/GC pauses) and wasteful (pads testIntegration runtime even when indexing finishes early), similar to fixed sleeps trunk commit 485496ad3e (PR #1805) already fixed in EntityTestSuite.java.

Since no writer-side synchronization hook exists, replace the fixed sleep with a bounded polling loop on the reader side (retry the search on a short interval, up to a generous timeout) in LuceneTests.groovy. Verify no flakiness across repeated testIntegration runs before landing.

description:
ServiceGroupReader.readConfig() (framework/service/src/main/java/org/apache/ofbiz/service/group/ServiceGroupReader.java:47) has no cache-hit guard, so it re-parses every component's service-group XML on each call. Its sibling getGroupModel() (line 99) already guards with "if (GROUPS_CACHE.isEmpty()) readConfig();", but readConfig() itself doesn't. It's called unconditionally from ServiceDispatcher's constructor on every dispatcher construction, so a full testIntegration run re-parses this XML dozens of times for no reason. Fix: add the same empty-cache guard inside readConfig(). GROUPS_CACHE is a plain ConcurrentHashMap and there's no evidence of a concurrent-mutation race here (unlike the ServiceEcaUtil case), so no locking is needed.

Also checked ServiceMcaUtil.getServiceMcaRules() (framework/service/src/main/java/org/apache/ofbiz/service/mail/ServiceMcaUtil.java:84) for the same issue. It already has an unsynchronized guard, but it's only called from JavaMailContainer (startup and mail-rule evaluation), not from ServiceDispatcher, so it's not on the same hot path and is left alone.

summary: Allow testIntegration to run with --portoffset for concurrent OFBiz test runs
description:
OFBiz's {{Start}} entrypoint already supports {{\-\-portoffset=<N>}}, which shifts every container's bound ports including the test Catalina container (hardcoded to 8010/8080/8443), but {{testIntegration}} has no way to pass it through: it hardcodes {{dependsOn 'ofbiz \-\-test'}}. Add an optional {{\-PportOffset}} Gradle property to {{testIntegration}} that appends {{\-\-portoffset=<N>}} to the underlying command when set, with no change in behavior when it's omitted, so multiple {{testIntegration}} runs (different branches, different worktrees, etc.) can run concurrently on the same machine without port conflicts.

Two pre-existing test bugs will block a clean run under a nonzero offset and need fixing alongside this: {{WidgetMacroLibraryTests}} and {{RestTestHttpRequest}} both hardcode {{localhost:8443}} URLs, and only one of six {{WidgetMacroLibraryTests}} methods self-corrects for a nonzero offset (a mutated instance field that doesn't survive JUnit's per-method fresh instance). Needs fixing on trunk; the same underlying bug, present at its pre-migration path, needs fixing on release24.09 too.

*Acceptance criteria:* a {{\-\-portoffset}} value passed via {{\-PportOffset}} reaches the test Catalina container's connectors; the default run (no property set) is unaffected; and two {{testIntegration}} runs at different offsets can run concurrently on the same machine without a port-bind conflict.

summary: Retry testIntegration once on non-graceful failure to absorb CI-worker flakiness
description:
BuildBot's {{ofbizTrunkFramework}} and {{ofbizBranch24Framework}} builders have hit roughly 10 sporadic {{GenericServiceException: Transaction has timed out}} failures in recent weeks, a different test each time. This has been traced to CI-worker resource contention from concurrent builds sharing a worker, not a code bug, and the underlying environmental cause is being pursued separately with Apache Infra.

Since the actual {{./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace testIntegration}} invocation is configured in Apache Infra's Buildbot master config rather than in this repo, retry logic cannot be added at that layer, so it needs to live inside the Gradle task itself.

This adds a single automatic retry to {{testIntegration}}, but only when the run does not complete gracefully, meaning a JVM crash, hang, or non-test container startup failure. A run that completes and legitimately reports one or more failing tests fails immediately, with no retry. {{TestRunContainer}} now writes a completion marker once every suite has run to completion and had its report written, which {{build.gradle}} uses to distinguish a graceful test failure from a run that never got the chance to finish.

This will also be backported to release24.09, since its {{ofbizBranch24Framework}} builder runs the identical {{testIntegration}} invocation and is affected by the same CI-worker contention, and since the fix touches only build and test tooling with no effect on shipped runtime behavior, backporting it ca

summary: Replace org.apache.commons:commons-imaging (stuck on alpha since 2019) with metadata-extractor + TwelveMonkeys ImageIO TIFF plugin
description: commons-imaging has been pinned to 1.0-alpha3 since its API broke in 1.0.0-alpha4; the project has stayed alpha-only since 2019 (currently 1.0.0-alpha6) with no GA in sight. An audit found real usage is concentrated in a single file, SecuredUpload.java, for two things: magic-byte format validation and a TIFF decode/encode fallback (PNG/GIF/JPEG are already handled by the JDK's built-in ImageIO). Both needs are covered without a new unproven dependency: metadata-extractor (already a project dependency) provides the same magic-byte detection via FileTypeDetector, and com.twelvemonkeys.imageio:imageio-tiff (pure-Java, BSD-3, actively maintained) gives ImageIO native TIFF support as a drop-in SPI plugin, letting the manual Commons Imaging fallback code be deleted outright. Net effect: one dependency removed, one narrow one added, ~70 fewer lines in the security-critical file. Patch ready on branch commons-imaging-replacement.

summary: ServiceDispatcher.localContext race causes intermittent NullPointerException in checkAuth/getLocalDispatcher
description:
ServiceDispatcher#localContext (a plain HashMap) is written under synchronized register()/deregister() but read without synchronization by getLocalContext(), getLocalDispatcher(), and containsContext() on every service invocation. Under concurrent dispatcher registration (many test suites constructing LocalDispatchers against the same delegator), HashMap.get() can intermittently return null for a key that is, and remains, registered, surfacing as a NullPointerException.

Same defect shape as the recent ServiceEcaUtil cache race fix, but in a sibling class that fix didn't touch, and predates it by about a month.

Evidence — Apache BuildBot ofbizBranch24Framework, marketingtests suite:
* Build #331 (2026-07-31, buildid 235388)
* Build #387 (2026-08-30, buildid 237853), MarketingTests.testCreateAndUpdateContactList

{code}
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.apache.ofbiz.service.DispatchContext.getSecurity()" because "dctx" is null
	at org.apache.ofbiz.service.ModelPermission.evalPermission(ModelPermission.java:80)
	at org.apache.ofbiz.service.ModelService.evalPermission(ModelService.java:1751)
	at org.apache.ofbiz.service.ServiceDispatcher.checkAuth(ServiceDispatcher.java:985)
	at org.apache.ofbiz.service.ServiceDispatcher.runSync(ServiceDispatcher.java:379)
{code}

Fix: switch localContext to a ConcurrentHashMap (register()/deregister() stay synchronized).

summary: Legacy jQuery.noConflict() in imagemanagement templates breaks common-theme JS (checkbox select-all, dialogs, category tree)
description: Five templates under applications/product/template/imagemanagement/ (ImageFrame.ftl, ImageRotating.ftl, ImageCrop.ftl, ResizeImage.ftl, ShowPeopleApprove.ftl) call jQuery.noConflict(), unchanged since 2010, which resets the global $ alias since nothing else in the theme uses it. OfbizUtil.js's initializeEvents() and importLibrary's cachedScript helper both reference bare $ in callbacks that run after page load, so once noConflict() fires they throw TypeError: $ is not a function and TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'extend'). This breaks checkbox select-all, dialog/confirm popups, and any importLibrary-loaded widget on the page, including the category tree and the page's own JS bundle (e.g. getJs?name=ImageFrame fails to load). Reproduced on Catalog Manager > Image Management > Manage > Frame action (catalog/control/checkAction?productId=...&contentId=...&dataResourceId=...). None of the five templates use bare $ themselves, they all call fully-qualified jQuery(...), so the noConflict() calls serve no purpose and should simply be removed.

summary: jGrowl toast messages use wrong readmore-js option (maxHeight instead of collapsedHeight)
description: showjGrowlMessage (OfbizUtil.js) initializes the vendored readmore-js plugin with maxHeight: 75, but readmore-js has no such option — the real option is collapsedHeight. summary: Introduce a Gradle version catalog for dependency versions
description:
Root dependencies.gradle declares ~80 dependency coordinates as scattered literal strings (e.g. implementation 'org.apache.poi:poi:5.5.1'), and settings.gradle pins two plugin versions the same way. No single source of truth exists for a version that repeats across multiple artifacts (e.g. log4j's 7 co-versioned modules), and no structured way to bump one.

Propose adding a Gradle version catalog (gradle/libs.versions.toml) — auto-detected by Gradle, wired into every subproject with no extra plumbing, usable since Gradle 7.4 (we've been on 7.6+ since OFBIZ-12400, Jan 2023) — and rewriting dependencies.gradle / settings.gradle to reference it instead of literals. Groups already sharing one version and configuration (jersey, swagger, batik, tika, pdfbox) get a bundles entry; the rest get individual libraries entries, sharing a versions key where a version repeats.

Out of scope: per-component build.gradle files (e.g. plugins/ldap's CAS dependency) keep declaring their own versions independently. No Dependabot config change needed — it already understands version catalogs natively.

Pure declaration-format refactor: no version bumps, no change to resolved dependencies or how they're downloaded.

Affected Components:
- dependencies.gradle
- settings.gradle
- gradle/libs.versions.toml (new)

Testing:
- Dependency-tree diff before/after the change, required to be identical.
- Full multi-project compile (./gradlew classes testClasses) — catches any typo'd alias.
